html:
Hans Christian Andersen was a Danish writer, born poor in Odense in 1805, whose fairy tales are read around the world.

He went to Copenhagen at fourteen hoping to be an actor or singer. Patrons paid for his schooling, and he wrote plays, novels and travel books. From 1835 he began publishing fairy tales, some retold from folk stories and many his own: The Little Mermaid, The Ugly Duckling, The Emperor's New Clothes, The Snow Queen, The Little Match Girl.

His tales mix humour with sadness and often speak for the outsider. They have been translated into more than a hundred languages and adapted endlessly in film. He is the best known Dane of the golden age of Danish culture, with Kierkegaard. Compare the earlier collections of the Brothers Grimm.
sum: Hans Christian Andersen was a Danish writer, born poor in Odense in 1805, whose fairy tales are read around the world.
